title: Redwood PLG Quickstart Discovery - Helix AI
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-11
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Sam (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (CTO, Helix), Rafael (ML Eng), Lena (PM)

Summary: quick PLG/self-serve discovery to understand Helix's dev experience needs, time-to-first-token, free credits, and whether hosted vs dedicated/private deployment is needed. Customer asked about security compliance (SOC2/KMS), VPC options, and pilot next steps.

[00:00] Sam: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm sam briggs from redwood inference, i'm the AE on this account, with priya our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Maya: good, thanks. excited to learn more. we're evaluating a few options for our product team to iterate fast.
[00:12] Priya: awesome, quick agenda, we'll cover quickstart experience, free credits / trial org, typical time-to-first-token, then touch on dedicated/private options and security. then open q&a and next steps. sound good?
[00:23] Lena: yep that's perfect.
[00:27] Rafael: yes, we'll mainly be focused on throughput and cost for embedding / chat use cases.
[00:35] Sam: great, super brief context question — what's your current stack for inference? are you running anything in prod?
[00:40] Maya: currently we have a couple small in-house endpoints on k8s using gpus on aws, but it's brittle. for now most prototyping is done with openai experimental because it was fastest to spin up.
[00:52] Rafael: prototypes use OpenAI and some local gptq desks for latency testing. our main ask is: can developers get started quickly, and then move to reserved capacity if performance/cost requires it.
[01:05] Priya: that aligns with what many teams do. Redwood has a quickstart path — you sign up, you get free credits, there's a sample repo and an SDK and you can get your first token in under 10 minutes. do you have SSO / SAML or will this be a small team pilot?
[01:20] Maya: pilot is 3-4 engineers + product for now, SSO later. security is important though, we need SOC2 and KMS support if we go beyond pilot.
[01:30] Sam: totally. we are SOC 2 compliant; for private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs. for hosted we have encrypted at rest and can integrate with enterprise key management for dedicated/private.
[01:42] Rafael: are there any gotchas around the quickstart with regards to data retention? we don't want logs retained beyond trial unless we opt-in.
[01:50] Priya: by default trial orgs keep minimal logs and you can request retention changes; security docs cover retention policies. we'll share the security pack.
[02:00] Lena: on the free credits — how much do you provide and what's a typical experiment cost?
[02:05] Sam: for PLG quickstarts we usually provide $500 in credits for 30 days for evaluation, enough to run a few hundred thousand tokens of testing, enough to test latency/cost and smoke integration.
[02:15] Maya: good, that sounds workable. for time-to-first-token — can you give specifics? we've seen some platforms where SDK setup took half a day.
[02:24] Priya: typical flow: create trial org -> API key -> install SDK (pip/npm) -> run sample script. with our quickstart templates and a postman collection many teams get first token under 10 minutes. if you want to test an on-prem model we can provide docker images but that adds setup.
[02:42] Rafael: and for latency profiling can we run benchmarks against your hosted endpoints?
[02:47] Priya: yes, we provide a benchmark harness and can help run perf tests. hosted endpoints show published latency profiles by model; for more precise numbers we'll run a short benchmark with your prompt set.
[02:58] Maya: ok, priorities for us are: fast dev experience, predictable cost, and a path to private deployment for regulatory workloads later. what are the tradeoffs between hosted, dedicated, and private?
[03:11] Sam: short version — hosted = fastest to start, variable multi-tenant capacity, lowest engineering overhead; dedicated = reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and better isolation, SLA-backed; private = VPC or on-prem, customer-managed networking and keys for regulated data. cost goes up from hosted -> dedicated -> private, but control increases as well.
[03:30] Rafael: can we start on hosted and move to dedicated without code changes?
[03:34] Priya: yes, the API and SDK remain the same. routing, instance types, and model variants are configurable in the console. you can pin model versions and rollout policies.
[03:45] Lena: curious about quantization and cost — do you advise on model selection/quantization?
[03:50] Priya: yes, Redwood Optimize provides recommendations: batching, quant profiles, and model variants by workload. our SEs will run initial cost/perf analysis.
[03:59] Rafael: security question — do you support VPC peering and private subnets for dedicated?
[04:04] Sam: dedicated supports VPC connections and private networking; private deployment gives you a customer-managed control plane or an on-prem bundle if needed.
[04:12] Maya: regarding compliance we have an internal checklist: SOC2, audit logs, SSO, IP allowlist, retention controls, and KMS. anything on that list unsupported?
[04:22] Priya: all supported — audit logs, RBAC, SAML/SSO flows, IP allowlist and KMS integration available in dedicated/private. we'll send the security pack with details.
[04:33] Sam: another note — many enterprise customers start with PLG flow and then sign a reserved capacity contract once throughput is proven. pricing and reserve levels depend on GPU specs and quantization choices.
[04:45] Rafael: can we get an example pricing sheet for reserved capacity and expected cost per 1M tokens?
[04:50] Sam: yes, we'll share a modelled pricing sheet along with sample ROI numbers based on embeddings/chat throughput.
[04:57] Lena: thanks. next, integration specifics: do you have base templates for vector stores / embeddings pipelines?
[05:05] Priya: yes, quickstart repo includes examples for FAISS, Pinecone, Milvus, and calls to our embeddings endpoint. it also includes a demo of prefix caching and suggested batching parameters.
[05:17] Rafael: great. for pilot success criteria we want: (1) devs can get first token in < 1 hour, (2) embeddings throughput > X QPS, (3) cost estimate for 6-month run. can you help define measurable metrics?
[05:29] Sam: absolutely; we'll work with you to define a success template and a short POC script for benchmarking.
[05:36] Maya: timeline — we'd like to start pilot next week if possible. is that realistic?
[05:40] Priya: yes, we can kick off trial org and credits within 24-48 hours. SE can run an initial perf run with your sample prompts within a week.
[05:48] Sam: ok i'll send invite for trial org and the quickstart repo link; priya will follow up to schedule a 60-minute technical demo and a benchmark session.
[05:56] Lena: perfect. any blockers from your side?
[05:59] Maya: only internal approvals for trial credits, but that's minor.
[06:02] Rafael: one more technical Q — what's the KV cache behavior with long-context models? we saw issues with memory at 32k in another provider.
[06:10] Priya: runtime handles KV cache in chunks and supports continuous batching and eviction policies. we can show cache metrics in the console and tune chunk sizes to avoid memory blowups.
[06:21] Sam: ok let's recap, i'll list action items and next steps.
[06:25] Priya: q&a?
[06:27] Maya: none from me.

Recap / Next Steps:
- Sam: create trial org and provision $500 credits for Helix AI; send quickstart repo and postman collection.
- Priya: schedule a technical demo and perf benchmarking session (60 min) with Rafael and team next week.
- Sam: send pricing / reserved capacity example and security pack (SOC2 docs, KMS, retention policy).
- Helix: confirm internal approvals and provide a small representative prompt set for benchmarking.

Action Items:
- "Sam Briggs: Provision trial org + $500 credits and send quickstart links by 2026-03-13"
- "Priya Nair: Schedule and run technical demo + perf benchmark session by 2026-03-18"
- "Sam Briggs: Send reserved capacity pricing sheet and security pack (SOC2/KMS docs) by 2026-03-14"
- "Maya Chen: Share representative prompts and confirm internal approval by 2026-03-15"

References / Links Mentioned:
- Quickstart repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstart (demo link)
- Security pack: /docs/security/soc2_kms_v1.pdf (will be shared)
- Benchmark harness: https://internal.redwood/bench/harness (SE link)

End of transcript
